---
title: "The multi-page subsystem"
---

A directory with a `_site.yml` is a **project**: a website or a book. The core's
`site/` module owns everything the
single-page path never had, the project-level concerns, while the per-page server
that drives it lives in [the dev server](server.qmd). This chapter is the core
subsystem: discovery, the config model, the front-matter primitives, link
rewriting, cross-page references, and search.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-site-render
%%| fig-cap: "A directory is discovered once; each page then runs through the shared core pipeline plus the site-only steps."
flowchart TB
  dir[("directory:<br/>_site.yml + .qmd pages")] --> disc["Site::discover<br/>config · pages · order · xref registry · search index"]
  disc --> page["per page · render_page"]
  page --> core["core pipeline<br/>(.qmd → blocks → HTML)"]
  core --> fm["expand front-matter blocks<br/>about: / hero: / listing:"]
  fm --> chrome["wrap in chrome<br/>navbar / footer / sidebar / prev-next"]
  chrome --> links["rewrite .qmd→.html<br/>+ resolve cross-page xrefs"]
  links --> out["page HTML"]
```

## Discovery

Drop `post.qmd` into a `posts/` folder beside a `_site.yml` and it joins a
website. `Site::discover` reads the root `_site.yml`, then walks the directory for
input pages: every `.qmd` becomes a page, **skipping `_`-prefixed directories**
(partials, `_freeze`, `_site`) and dotfiles. Each page maps to its output URL (`x.qmd` →
`x.html`, mirroring the input tree). Both `build` (static) and `preview` (live) drive a
project through the same `discover` + `render_page`.

Two kinds of `.qmd` are discovered but deliberately kept out of the navigable page set: a
`draft: true` page is excluded from a **website** entirely (no output, nav, listing, or
prev/next entry; books do not consult `draft`), and a deck pulled in by
`{{< embed >}}` is built and served but stays out of nav and search, since it is an
inclusion, not a page. A loose `format: revealjs` file that no page embeds warns rather
than silently becoming a chrome-wrapped article.

## The config model

The typed `SiteConfig` is qmd-fast's **native, flat** schema (title, nav, footer,
`mounts:`, ...). Config is deliberately **two levels with no cascade**: the root
`_site.yml` sets project-wide defaults and a page's own front matter overrides
them, full stop. There is no `_metadata.yml` directory merge, the single most
confusing part of Quarto's model.

The schema is a **closed set**: an unknown top-level key warns with a "did you
mean" hint (`config/mod.rs` `validate_keys`). A Quarto-shaped nested config
(`project:` / `website:` / `book:` / `format:`) is no longer accepted: those keys
warn as unknown and their nested values are ignored, so a Quarto config must be
flattened to the native shape.

qmd-fast generates a JSON Schema for `_site.yml` from `NATIVE_KEYS` (the same
closed set the config validator uses), emitted by `qmd-fast schema`. See the
Configuration reference (`../guide/reference/configuration.html`) for the editor
autocomplete on-ramp.

## Books vs websites

The same machinery produces both, branched on one key: **`chapters:` present ⇒ a
book** (a left chapter sidebar, numbered chapters + sections, prev/next-*chapter*
navigation), otherwise a website (a top navbar). `book.rs` computes
the section numbers that the sidebar and cross-references display. No `type:` is
needed; the shape of the config decides. A `chapters:` entry is a bare path, a
`{ part:, chapters: }` group, or a `{ file:, text: }` mapping whose `text:`
overrides the sidebar label (otherwise the label is the chapter's first `# H1`).

## Front-matter primitives

Three front-matter blocks turn a page into something structured, and all three
render into the **framework's own primitives with no bespoke HTML**, the same
primitives the marketing site is built from:

- **`about:`** replaces the title block with a centered profile header (image, name,
  links).
- **`hero:`** replaces it with the `.hero` band (eyebrow, headline, lead, CTA
  buttons). `about:` and `hero:` are mutually exclusive, both stand in for the
  title.
- **`listing:`** crawls a `contents:` directory and emits a card per document (image,
  date, title, description, categories), sorted by date and capped, as a grid or a
  stacked list, so a blog index or a projects page generates from front matter.

## Cross-page links and references

Two related rewrites stitch the pages together:

- **Link rewriting.** Intra-site `.qmd` links (including `other.qmd#anchor`) are
  rewritten to their built `.html` targets, so the source links the way you'd type
  it and the output links correctly.
- **Cross-page cross-references** (`xref.rs`). A project-wide registry scans every
  page for `{#sec-}` / `{#fig-}` / … anchors (plus a section number for numbered book
  sections), then rewrites `data-qmd-xref`-marked links to point at the right page.
  So a `@fig-` in one chapter resolves, with its number, to its figure in another.

## Full-text search

`search.rs` builds **one cross-page index**: every page's title and each anchored
heading, each carrying the **plain-text body of its section**, so Cmd-K matches
prose, not just headings. It is built once at discovery and **written to a separate
`search.json`, lazy-loaded by the client on first open**, rather than inlined into
every page, so the index never bloats page weight. (On a 17-page book that saved
over a megabyte across the pages.) The palette is opened by the navbar search
control (or the book sidebar's, for a book) or the <kbd>Cmd/Ctrl-K</kbd> shortcut.

## Social & SEO metadata

Each page emits OpenGraph, Twitter-card, and `canonical` tags (`meta.rs`), taken from the
page's own front matter (`title`, `description`, `image`) and falling back to the
`_site.yml` config. `og:type` is `article` when the page carries a `date:`, and `website`
otherwise. The absolute-URL tags (`og:url`, `og:image`, `canonical`) are emitted **only
when a `url:` is configured**, since social scrapers need absolute URLs; without a `url:`
the page still carries its relative title/description metadata.

## Mounts

`mounts:` serves *another* project under a URL prefix in `preview`, which is how the
marketing site resolves its `/docs/guide` and `/docs/internals` links live. Under
`preview` a mounted page is **rendered on request as static output**, so it has no live
websocket, no dev menu, and no click-to-source; to edit a mounted book with the full live
loop, preview it directly (`preview docs/internals`) rather than through the mount.

The static `build` does **not** auto-wire mounts: building the site emits each page and its
own assets, but a `mounts:` sub-project is a separate project, so `build <site>` only
*warns* (naming each mount and the exact command) rather than producing it. Build each mount
yourself into the matching sub-path, e.g. `qmd-fast build docs/internals --out _site/docs/internals`,
so the deployed `/docs/internals/` links resolve. (Auto-building mounts is a planned
follow-up.)
